hook: Xiangyu Zhang enrolled at Xi'an Jiaotong University in 2008 and completed a bachelor's degree in software engineering in 2012. He then entered a joint PhD program between Xi'an Jiaotong University and Microsoft Research Asia, working under Jian Sun and Kaiming He. As part of that team he co-authored Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition in 2015, contributing the underlying framework and implementation for what became known as ResNet, a network design that let researchers train models hundreds of layers deep. He later worked as a Principal Researcher at Megvii, where in 2017 and 2018 he led the development of ShuffleNet, a convolutional architecture designed specifically to run efficiently on mobile devices with limited computing power. According to industry reporting, he subsequently joined the Chinese large language model company StepFun as Chief Scientist.
name: Xiangyu Zhang

quote.text: We introduce an extremely computation-efficient CNN architecture named ShuffleNet, which is designed specially for mobile devices with very limited computing power.
quote.context: From the abstract of the 2018 paper "ShuffleNet: An Extremely Efficient Convolutional Neural Network for Mobile Devices," co-authored with Xinyu Zhou, Mengxiao Lin, and Jian Sun.

ShuffleNet: An Extremely Efficient Convolutional Neural Network for Mobile Devices (CVPR 2018)

timeline.event: Completed a BEng in software engineering and began a joint PhD program with Microsoft Research Asia under Jian Sun and Kaiming He.
Co-authored "Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition" with Kaiming He, Shaoqing Ren, and Jian Sun.
timeline.impact: Provided the implementation work behind ResNet, whose residual connections became foundational to deep computer vision models.

timeline.event: Began work on ShuffleNet at Megvii as a Principal Researcher.
timeline.impact: Focused his research on making deep networks efficient enough to run on mobile hardware.

timeline.event: Published "ShuffleNet: An Extremely Efficient Convolutional Neural Network for Mobile Devices" with Xinyu Zhou, Mengxiao Lin, and Jian Sun.
timeline.impact: Delivered one of the most widely used efficient CNN architectures for on-device computer vision.

timeline.event: Reported by industry press to have joined the large language model company StepFun as Chief Scientist.
timeline.impact: Extended his research focus from computer vision architectures into large-scale generative models.

Wrote the underlying framework and code for the original ResNet paper
Led development of ShuffleNet, an efficient mobile CNN architecture, in 2017 to 2018
Worked as a Principal Researcher at Megvii

achievements.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition (2015)
achievements.impact: Co-authored ResNet, contributing the framework and coding that made it possible to train networks hundreds of layers deep, a design that remains a default building block across computer vision.

achievements.title: ShuffleNet (2018)
achievements.impact: Designed an extremely efficient convolutional architecture for mobile devices, influencing efficient neural network design used in smartphone applications such as facial recognition.

achievements.title: RepVGG
achievements.impact: Contributed to structural re-parameterization techniques that simplify network architecture at inference time without sacrificing accuracy.
